questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A distress flare is fired from the ground such that it reaches a maximum vertical height of $21.6 \text{ m}$. If the angle of projection was $60^{\circ}$ with the horizontal, what was the initial speed of the flare? (Take $g = 10 \text{ m/s}^2$ and neglect air resistance)
questions.solution:
The maximum height $H$ of a projectile is given by the formula:

$H = \dfrac{u^2 \sin^2 \theta}{2g}$

Substituting the given values $H = 21.6 \text{ m}$, $\theta = 60^{\circ}$, and $g = 10 \text{ m/s}^2$:

$21.6 = \dfrac{u^2 \sin^2 60^{\circ}}{2 \times 10}$

$21.6 = \dfrac{u^2 \left(\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)^2}{20}$

$21.6 = \dfrac{3u^2}{80}$

$u^2 = \dfrac{21.6 \times 80}{3}$

$u^2 = \dfrac{1728}{3} = 576$

$u = 24 \text{ m/s}$

Answer: $24 \text{ m/s}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
Three blocks of masses $m_1 = 5\text{ kg}$, $m_2 = 3\text{ kg}$, and $m_3 = 2\text{ kg}$ are placed in contact with each other on a frictionless horizontal surface. A constant horizontal force $F_1 = 50\text{ N}$ is applied on $m_1$ to the right, and another constant horizontal force $F_2 = 10\text{ N}$ is applied on $m_3$ to the left, as shown in the figure.

What is the ratio of the normal contact force between $m_1$ and $m_2$ to the normal contact force between $m_2$ and $m_3$?
questions.solution:
Let the common acceleration of the system be $a$.

The net force on the system is $F_{\text{net}} = F_1 - F_2 = 50 - 10 = 40\text{ N}$.

Total mass of the system is $M = m_1 + m_2 + m_3 = 5 + 3 + 2 = 10\text{ kg}$.

The acceleration is $a = \dfrac{F_{\text{net}}}{M} = \dfrac{40}{10} = 4\text{ m/s}^2$.

Let $N_1$ be the normal contact force between $m_1$ and $m_2$. Considering the free body diagram of $m_1$:

$F_1 - N_1 = m_1 a$

$50 - N_1 = 5 \times 4$

$N_1 = 30\text{ N}$

Let $N_2$ be the normal contact force between $m_2$ and $m_3$. Considering the free body diagram of $m_3$:

$N_2 - F_2 = m_3 a$

$N_2 - 10 = 2 \times 4$

$N_2 = 18\text{ N}$

The ratio of the normal contact forces is $\dfrac{N_1}{N_2} = \dfrac{30}{18} = \dfrac{5}{3}$.

Answer: $5 : 3$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
A small block of mass $m$ is moved from point $P(0,0)$ to point $Q(R, R)$ in a vertical $xy$-plane (where the $y$-axis is vertical). The block is moved along three different paths as shown in the figure:

Path 1: Along the circular arc $PQ$ of radius $R$ centered at $O(0, R)$.
Path 2: Along the horizontal line $PS$ to $S(R, 0)$ and then vertically to $Q$.
Path 3: Along the vertical line $PO$ to $O(0, R)$ and then horizontally to $Q$.

If $W_1, W_2$, and $W_3$ represent the work done by the gravitational force on the block along paths 1, 2, and 3 respectively, which of the following relations is correct?
questions.solution:
The gravitational force is a conservative force. The work done by a conservative force depends only on the initial and final positions of the particle and is independent of the path taken.

Here, the initial point is $P(0, 0)$ and the final point is $Q(R, R)$. The vertical displacement of the block is $\Delta y = R - 0 = R$.

The work done by the gravitational force along any path between these two points is given by:
$W = -mg \Delta y = -mgR$

Since all three paths 1, 2, and 3 have the same initial and final points, the work done by gravity is the same for all of them.

Therefore, $W_1 = W_2 = W_3$.

Answer: $W_1 = W_2 = W_3$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A bullet of mass $20 \text{ g}$ is moving with a constant linear momentum of $8 \text{ kg m/s}$. The time taken by the bullet to cover a straight distance of $120 \text{ m}$ is:
questions.solution:
Given mass of the bullet, $m = 20 \text{ g} = 20 \times 10^{-3} \text{ kg}$

Linear momentum, $p = 8 \text{ kg m/s}$

Velocity of the bullet, $v = \dfrac{p}{m} = \dfrac{8}{20 \times 10^{-3}} = 400 \text{ m/s}$

Distance to be covered, $d = 120 \text{ m}$

Time taken, $t = \dfrac{d}{v} = \dfrac{120}{400} = 0.3 \text{ s}$

Answer: $0.3 \text{ s}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
A uniform solid cylinder of mass $20 \text{ kg}$ and radius $0.5 \text{ m}$ is rotating about its central axis. The amount of work required to increase its angular speed from $120 \text{ rpm}$ to $300 \text{ rpm}$ is:
(Take $\pi^2 = 10$)
questions.solution:
Moment of inertia of the solid cylinder about its central axis is $I = \dfrac{1}{2}mr^2$

Substituting the given values:

$I = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 20 \times (0.5)^2 = 2.5 \text{ kg m}^2$

Initial angular speed, $\omega_1 = 120 \text{ rpm} = 120 \times \dfrac{2\pi}{60} = 4\pi \text{ rad/s}$

Final angular speed, $\omega_2 = 300 \text{ rpm} = 300 \times \dfrac{2\pi}{60} = 10\pi \text{ rad/s}$

According to the work-energy theorem, the work required is equal to the change in rotational kinetic energy:

$W = \dfrac{1}{2}I(\omega_2^2 - \omega_1^2)$

$W = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 2.5 \times ((10\pi)^2 - (4\pi)^2)$

$W = 1.25 \times (100\pi^2 - 16\pi^2)$

$W = 1.25 \times 84\pi^2$

Given $\pi^2 = 10$:

$W = 1.25 \times 84 \times 10 = 1050 \text{ J}$

Answer: $1050 \text{ J}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Consider two open water tanks, Tank X and Tank Y, both completely filled with water. Tank X has a stepped shape: its upper section is a cylinder of radius $2R$ and height $h$, while its lower section is a cylinder of radius $R$ and height $h$. Tank Y is a uniform cylinder of radius $R$ and total height $2h$. If $P_X$ and $P_Y$ represent the hydrostatic gauge pressure at the bottom-most points of Tank X and Tank Y respectively, which of the following relations is correct?
questions.solution:
The hydrostatic gauge pressure at a depth $H$ in a liquid of density $\rho$ is given by $P = \rho g H$. It depends only on the vertical depth from the free surface and is independent of the shape of the container.

For Tank X, the total vertical depth of water from the free surface to the bottom-most point is $h + h = 2h$.
Therefore, the gauge pressure at the bottom of Tank X is:
$P_X = \rho g (2h)$

For Tank Y, the total vertical depth of water from the free surface to the bottom-most point is $2h$.
Therefore, the gauge pressure at the bottom of Tank Y is:
$P_Y = \rho g (2h)$

Comparing the two pressures, we get:
$P_X = P_Y$

Answer: $P_X = P_Y$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A small plastic sphere of diameter $4 \text{ mm}$ is observed to fall with a constant terminal velocity of $5 \text{ cm s}^{-1}$ through a tall jar containing a viscous liquid. If the coefficient of viscosity of the liquid is $0.2 \text{ N s m}^{-2}$, what is the magnitude of the viscous drag force acting on the sphere? (Take $\pi = 3.14$)
questions.solution:
According to Stokes' law, the viscous drag force $F$ acting on a spherical body of radius $r$ falling with terminal velocity $v$ through a fluid of viscosity $\eta$ is given by:

$F = 6 \pi \eta r v$

Given:
Radius of the sphere, $r = \dfrac{4 \text{ mm}}{2} = 2 \times 10^{-3} \text{ m}$
Terminal velocity, $v = 5 \text{ cm s}^{-1} = 5 \times 10^{-2} \text{ m s}^{-1}$
Coefficient of viscosity, $\eta = 0.2 \text{ N s m}^{-2}$

Substituting the values into the formula:

$F = 6 \times 3.14 \times 0.2 \times (2 \times 10^{-3}) \times (5 \times 10^{-2})$

$F = 6 \times 3.14 \times 0.2 \times 10 \times 10^{-5}$

$F = 12 \times 3.14 \times 10^{-5}$

$F = 37.68 \times 10^{-5} \text{ N}$

$F = 3.768 \times 10^{-4} \text{ N} \approx 3.77 \times 10^{-4} \text{ N}$

Answer: $3.77 \times 10^{-4} \text{ N}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The displacement $x(t)$ of a particle moving along a straight line is given by various mathematical functions of time $t$. Which of the following functions represents a motion that is NOT periodic?
questions.solution:
For a function to represent periodic motion, it must repeat its values after a regular interval of time.

Option (A): $x(t) = A \sin^3(\omega t) = \dfrac{A}{4} (3 \sin(\omega t) - \sin(3\omega t))$. This is a sum of periodic functions, hence it is periodic.

Option (B): $x(t) = A \cos(\omega t) + B \sin(\omega t) = \sqrt{A^2+B^2} \sin(\omega t + \phi)$. This represents simple harmonic motion, which is periodic.

Option (C): $x(t) = A \log(\omega t)$. The logarithmic function is strictly increasing for $t \gt 0$ and never repeats its values. Hence, it is not periodic.

Option (D): $x(t) = A \cos^2(\omega t) = \dfrac{A}{2} (1 + \cos(2\omega t))$. This is a periodic function with period $\dfrac{\pi}{\omega}$.

Therefore, $x(t) = A \log(\omega t)$ represents a motion that is not periodic.

Answer: $x(t) = A \log(\omega t)$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A parallel plate air capacitor has an initial capacitance of $12 \text{ pF}$. If the separation between its plates is reduced to one-third of its original value and the area of each plate is doubled, what will be the new capacitance?
questions.solution:
The capacitance of a parallel plate capacitor is given by $C = \dfrac{\varepsilon_0 A}{d}$

Given initial capacitance $C_1 = \dfrac{\varepsilon_0 A}{d} = 12 \text{ pF}$

The new area is $A' = 2A$ and the new separation is $d' = \dfrac{d}{3}$

The new capacitance is $C_2 = \dfrac{\varepsilon_0 A'}{d'} = \dfrac{\varepsilon_0 (2A)}{\dfrac{d}{3}} = 6 \dfrac{\varepsilon_0 A}{d}$

$C_2 = 6 C_1 = 6 \times 12 \text{ pF} = 72 \text{ pF}$

Answer: $72 \text{ pF}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two unknown capacitors are connected across a $10 \mathrm{~V}$ DC supply. When they are connected in parallel, the total charge drawn from the supply is $250 \mu \mathrm{C}$. When they are connected in series across the same supply, the total charge drawn is $40 \mu \mathrm{C}$. The individual capacitances of the two capacitors are:
questions.solution:
Let the capacitances be $C_1$ and $C_2$.

When connected in parallel, the equivalent capacitance is $C_p = C_1 + C_2$.
The total charge drawn is $Q_p = C_p V$.
$(C_1 + C_2) \times 10 = 250$
$C_1 + C_2 = 25 \mu \mathrm{F}$

When connected in series, the equivalent capacitance is $C_s = \dfrac{C_1 C_2}{C_1 + C_2}$.
The total charge drawn is $Q_s = C_s V$.
$\dfrac{C_1 C_2}{C_1 + C_2} \times 10 = 40$
$\dfrac{C_1 C_2}{25} \times 10 = 40$
$C_1 C_2 = 100 (\mu \mathrm{F})^2$

Solving the equations $C_1 + C_2 = 25$ and $C_1 C_2 = 100$, we get a quadratic equation:
$C^2 - 25C + 100 = 0$
$(C - 20)(C - 5) = 0$

Thus, the individual capacitances are $20 \mu \mathrm{F}$ and $5 \mu \mathrm{F}$.

Answer: $20 \mu \mathrm{F}, 5 \mu \mathrm{F}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A car battery has an electromotive force of $12 \text{ V}$ and an internal resistance of $0.4 \Omega$. When it is connected to a headlight of resistance $5.6 \Omega$, what is the potential difference across the terminals of the battery?
questions.solution:
Given electromotive force $E = 12 \text{ V}$, internal resistance $r = 0.4 \Omega$, and external resistance $R = 5.6 \Omega$.

The current in the circuit is given by $I = \dfrac{E}{R + r}$.

Substituting the given values, $I = \dfrac{12}{5.6 + 0.4} = \dfrac{12}{6.0} = 2 \text{ A}$.

The potential difference across the terminals of the battery is $V = IR$.

Substituting the values, $V = 2 \times 5.6 = 11.2 \text{ V}$.

Answer: $11.2 \text{ V}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
In the circuit shown below, two non-ideal cells are connected in parallel across an external resistor $R = 2\Omega$. Cell 1 has an emf $E_1 = 8\text{ V}$ and internal resistance $r_1 = 1\Omega$. Cell 2 has an emf $E_2 = 4\text{ V}$ and internal resistance $r_2 = 2\Omega$. Both cells are connected with their positive terminals to the same upper junction.

Which of the following correctly describes the magnitude of the current passing through Cell 2 and its operational state?
questions.solution:
Let the potential of the lower junction be $0\text{ V}$ and the upper junction be $V$.

Applying Kirchhoff's Current Law at the upper junction:

$\dfrac{V - 8}{1} + \dfrac{V - 4}{2} + \dfrac{V}{2} = 0$

Multiplying the equation by $2$:

$2(V - 8) + (V - 4) + V = 0$

$2V - 16 + V - 4 + V = 0$

$4V = 20 \Rightarrow V = 5\text{ V}$

The current through Cell 2 is:

$I_2 = \dfrac{V - E_2}{r_2} = \dfrac{5 - 4}{2} = 0.5\text{ A}$

Since $V \gt E_2$, the current flows from the upper junction into the positive terminal of Cell 2. Therefore, Cell 2 is being charged.

Answer: $0.5\text{ A}$, being charged

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
A steady current of $10\text{ A}$ is flowing through a wire which is bent into the shape of a circular arc of radius $5\text{ cm}$. If the arc subtends an angle of $90^{\circ}$ at its centre, what is the magnitude of the magnetic field produced at the centre of the arc?

(Assume permeability of free space, $\mu_0 = 4\pi \times 10^{-7}\text{ T}\cdot\text{m/A}$)
questions.solution:
The magnetic field at the centre of a circular arc subtending an angle $\theta$ is given by $B = \dfrac{\mu_0 I}{4\pi r} \theta$.

Given $I = 10\text{ A}$, $r = 5\text{ cm} = 0.05\text{ m}$, and $\theta = 90^{\circ} = \dfrac{\pi}{2}$ radians.

Substituting the values:

$B = \dfrac{4\pi \times 10^{-7} \times 10}{4\pi \times 0.05} \times \dfrac{\pi}{2}$

$B = \dfrac{10^{-6}}{0.05} \times \dfrac{\pi}{2}$

$B = \dfrac{\pi \times 10^{-6}}{0.1}$

$B = \pi \times 10^{-5}\text{ T}$

Answer: $\pi \times 10^{-5}\text{ T}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A long straight vertical wire carries a steady current directed vertically upward. What is the direction of the magnetic field at a point located horizontally to the south of the wire?
questions.solution:
According to the right-hand thumb rule, if we point the thumb of our right hand in the direction of the current (vertically upward), our curled fingers indicate the direction of the magnetic field lines.

The magnetic field lines form concentric circles around the wire in a counterclockwise direction when viewed from above.

Let the wire be along the z-axis with the current flowing in the $+z$ direction (upward). Let North be the $+y$ direction, South be the $-y$ direction, East be the $+x$ direction, and West be the $-x$ direction.

The position vector of a point to the south of the wire is $\vec{r} = -r \hat{j}$.

The direction of the magnetic field is given by the cross product of the current direction and the position vector: $\hat{k} \times (-\hat{j}) = \hat{i}$.

The direction $\hat{i}$ corresponds to East. Therefore, the magnetic field at a point located to the south of the wire is directed towards East.

Answer: Towards East

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A coil is connected to a $20\text{ V}$ DC supply and draws a steady current of $5\text{ A}$. When the same coil is connected to a $20\text{ V}$, $\dfrac{50}{\pi}\text{ Hz}$ AC supply, it draws an rms current of $4\text{ A}$. The resistance and the inductance of the coil are respectively:
questions.solution:
For a DC supply, the frequency is zero, so the inductive reactance is zero. The steady current is limited only by the resistance of the coil.

$R = \dfrac{V_{DC}}{I_{DC}} = \dfrac{20}{5} = 4\ \Omega$

For an AC supply, the impedance $Z$ of the coil limits the current.

$Z = \dfrac{V_{rms}}{I_{rms}} = \dfrac{20}{4} = 5\ \Omega$

The impedance of the coil is given by $Z = \sqrt{R^2 + X_L^2}$, where $X_L$ is the inductive reactance.

$5 = \sqrt{4^2 + X_L^2}$

$25 = 16 + X_L^2$

$X_L = 3\ \Omega$

The inductive reactance is $X_L = \omega L = 2\pi f L$.

$3 = 2\pi \left(\dfrac{50}{\pi}\right) L$

$3 = 100 L$

$L = \dfrac{3}{100}\text{ H} = 0.03\text{ H} = 30\text{ mH}$

The resistance is $4\ \Omega$ and the inductance is $30\text{ mH}$.

Answer: $4\ \Omega$, $30\text{ mH}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
An electric heating coil dissipates $1000 \mathrm{~W}$ of average power when operated on an a.c. source. If the peak value of the alternating current flowing through the coil is $10 \mathrm{~A}$, what is the rms voltage of the a.c. source?
(Assume the coil is purely resistive)
questions.solution:
Average power dissipated in a purely resistive circuit is given by $P = V_{rms} I_{rms}$.

The rms current is related to the peak current by $I_{rms} = \dfrac{I_0}{\sqrt{2}}$.

Substituting the given peak current $I_0 = 10 \mathrm{~A}$:

$I_{rms} = \dfrac{10}{\sqrt{2}} = 5\sqrt{2} \mathrm{~A}$

Using the power formula:

$1000 = V_{rms} \times 5\sqrt{2}$

$V_{rms} = \dfrac{1000}{5\sqrt{2}} = 100\sqrt{2} \mathrm{~V}$

Since $\sqrt{2} \approx 1.414$:

$V_{rms} = 100 \times 1.414 = 141.4 \mathrm{~V}$

Answer: $141.4 \mathrm{~V}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A plane electromagnetic wave is propagating through free space. If the peak value of the electric field in the wave is $E_0$, which of the following expressions correctly represents the peak value of the associated magnetic field $B_0$ in terms of the permeability ($\mu_0$) and permittivity ($\varepsilon_0$) of free space?
questions.solution:
The relationship between the peak electric field $E_0$ and the peak magnetic field $B_0$ in an electromagnetic wave propagating in free space is given by:

$E_0 = c B_0$

where $c$ is the speed of light in vacuum.

The speed of light is related to the permeability $\mu_0$ and permittivity $\varepsilon_0$ of free space by the equation:

$c = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{\mu_0 \varepsilon_0}}$

Substituting the value of $c$ into the first equation:

$E_0 = \dfrac{B_0}{\sqrt{\mu_0 \varepsilon_0}}$

Rearranging to solve for $B_0$:

$B_0 = E_0 \sqrt{\mu_0 \varepsilon_0}$

Answer: $E_0 \sqrt{\mu_0 \varepsilon_0}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Optical fibers are extensively used for transmitting audio and video signals over long distances without significant loss of intensity. Which of the following statements correctly describes the design principle and the optical phenomenon responsible for guiding light inside the fiber?
options: The core must have a higher refractive index than the cladding, and light is guided by successive refractions.
The core must have a lower refractive index than the cladding, and light is guided by total internal reflection.
The core must have a higher refractive index than the cladding, and light is guided by total internal reflection.
The core must have a lower refractive index than the cladding, and light is guided by successive refractions.
questions.solution:
Optical fibers operate on the principle of total internal reflection.

For total internal reflection to occur, light must travel from an optically denser medium to an optically rarer medium, and the angle of incidence must be greater than the critical angle.

Therefore, the core of the optical fiber must have a higher refractive index than the surrounding cladding.

Answer: The core must have a higher refractive index than the cladding, and light is guided by total internal reflection.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Unpolarized light of initial intensity $I_0$ is incident on a pair of polaroids. The first polaroid acts as a polarizer and the second as an analyzer. If the intensity of the light transmitted through the analyzer is $\dfrac{I_0}{4}$, what is the angle between the transmission axes of the two polaroids?
questions.solution:
Intensity of light after passing through the first polaroid is $I_1 = \dfrac{I_0}{2}$.

Let $\theta$ be the angle between the transmission axes of the two polaroids.

According to Malus's law, the intensity of light transmitted through the analyzer is $I_2 = I_1 \cos^2 \theta$.

Substituting the given values:

$\dfrac{I_0}{4} = \dfrac{I_0}{2} \cos^2 \theta$

$\cos^2 \theta = \dfrac{1}{2}$

$\cos \theta = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$

$\theta = 45^{\circ}$

Answer: $45^{\circ}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: If the radius of the third Bohr orbit of a hydrogen atom is $R$, then the radius of the second Bohr orbit of a $Be^{3+}$ ion will be:
questions.solution:
The radius of the $n$-th Bohr orbit for a hydrogen-like species is given by $r_n = r_0 \dfrac{n^2}{Z}$, where $r_0$ is the Bohr radius.

For the third Bohr orbit of a hydrogen atom ($n = 3, Z = 1$):

$R = r_0 \dfrac{3^2}{1} = 9 r_0$

$\Rightarrow r_0 = \dfrac{R}{9}$

For the second Bohr orbit of a $Be^{3+}$ ion ($n = 2, Z = 4$):

$r' = r_0 \dfrac{2^2}{4} = r_0 \dfrac{4}{4} = r_0$

Substituting the value of $r_0$, we get:

$r' = \dfrac{R}{9}$

Answer: $\dfrac{R}{9}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: An electron (mass $m_e$ ) and a proton (mass $m_p$ ) are initially at rest. Both particles are then accelerated through the exact same potential difference $V$. What is the ratio of the de Broglie wavelength of the electron to that of the proton $\left(\lambda_e / \lambda_p\right)$ ?
questions.solution:
The de Broglie wavelength of a particle is given by $\lambda = \dfrac{h}{p}$

The kinetic energy $K$ acquired by a particle of charge $q$ accelerated through a potential difference $V$ is $K = qV$

The momentum $p$ is related to kinetic energy by $p = \sqrt{2mK} = \sqrt{2mqV}$

For an electron and a proton, the magnitude of charge is the same, $q = e$

The de Broglie wavelengths are $\lambda_e = \dfrac{h}{\sqrt{2m_e eV}}$ and $\lambda_p = \dfrac{h}{\sqrt{2m_p eV}}$

Taking the ratio gives $\dfrac{\lambda_e}{\lambda_p} = \sqrt{\dfrac{m_p}{m_e}}$

Answer: $\sqrt{\dfrac{m_p} {m_e}}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The threshold wavelength for a certain photosensitive surface is $\lambda_0$. When light of wavelength $\dfrac{\lambda_0}{3}$ falls on it, the maximum kinetic energy of the ejected photoelectrons is:
questions.solution:
The work function of the photosensitive surface is given by $\Phi = \dfrac{hc}{\lambda_0}$.

The energy of the incident light of wavelength $\lambda = \dfrac{\lambda_0}{3}$ is $E = \dfrac{hc}{\lambda} = \dfrac{3hc}{\lambda_0}$.

According to Einstein's photoelectric equation, the maximum kinetic energy of the ejected photoelectrons is:

$K_{\text{max}} = E - \Phi$

$K_{\text{max}} = \dfrac{3hc}{\lambda_0} - \dfrac{hc}{\lambda_0} = \dfrac{2hc}{\lambda_0}$

Answer: $\dfrac{2hc}{\lambda_0}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The volume of a solid cylinder is calculated using the relation $V = \pi r^2 h$. If the radius $r$ is measured as $(2.0 \pm 0.02)\text{ cm}$ and the height $h$ is measured as $(5.0 \pm 0.1)\text{ cm}$, the maximum percentage error in the calculated volume is:
questions.solution:
The volume of a solid cylinder is given by $V = \pi r^2 h$.

The maximum percentage error in the volume is given by:

$\dfrac{\Delta V}{V} \times 100 = \left( 2 \dfrac{\Delta r}{r} + \dfrac{\Delta h}{h} \right) \times 100$

Given values are:

$r = 2.0\text{ cm}$, $\Delta r = 0.02\text{ cm}$

$h = 5.0\text{ cm}$, $\Delta h = 0.1\text{ cm}$

Substituting these values into the error formula:

$\dfrac{\Delta V}{V} \times 100 = \left( 2 \times \dfrac{0.02}{2.0} + \dfrac{0.1}{5.0} \right) \times 100$

$\dfrac{\Delta V}{V} \times 100 = (2 \times 0.01 + 0.02) \times 100$

$\dfrac{\Delta V}{V} \times 100 = (0.02 + 0.02) \times 100 = 0.04 \times 100 = 4\%$

Answer: $4\%$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
The position-time ($x-t$) graph of a particle moving along a straight line is shown in the figure. The graph is divided into three distinct segments: OP, PQ, and QR.

Which segment of the graph represents motion with negative acceleration?
questions.solution:
The slope of the position-time ($x-t$) graph represents the velocity of the particle, $v = \dfrac{dx}{dt}$.

The rate of change of this slope represents the acceleration, $a = \dfrac{d^2x}{dt^2}$.

In segment OP, the curve is concave upwards, indicating that the slope (velocity) is increasing. Hence, the acceleration is positive ($a \gt 0$).

In segment PQ, the graph is a straight line, indicating a constant slope (velocity). Hence, the acceleration is zero ($a = 0$).

In segment QR, the curve is concave downwards, indicating that the slope (velocity) is decreasing. Hence, the acceleration is negative ($a \lt 0$).

Therefore, segment QR represents motion with negative acceleration.

Answer: Segment QR

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The gravitational potential in a certain region of space is given by the expression $V = -x^{2}y^{3} + 3z^{2}$, where $V$ is in $\text{J/kg}$ and $x, y, z$ are in meters. What is the magnitude of the gravitational field intensity at the point $(1, 1, -1)\text{ m}$?
questions.solution:
The gravitational field intensity $\vec{E}$ is related to the gravitational potential $V$ by the relation:

$\vec{E} = -\left( \dfrac{\partial V}{\partial x} \hat{i} + \dfrac{\partial V}{\partial y} \hat{j} + \dfrac{\partial V}{\partial z} \hat{k} \right)$

Given $V = -x^{2}y^{3} + 3z^{2}$, we find the partial derivatives:

$\dfrac{\partial V}{\partial x} = -2xy^{3}$

$\dfrac{\partial V}{\partial y} = -3x^{2}y^{2}$

$\dfrac{\partial V}{\partial z} = 6z$

Evaluating these at the point $(1, 1, -1)$:

$\dfrac{\partial V}{\partial x} = -2(1)(1)^{3} = -2$

$\dfrac{\partial V}{\partial y} = -3(1)^{2}(1)^{2} = -3$

$\dfrac{\partial V}{\partial z} = 6(-1) = -6$

Substituting these values into the expression for $\vec{E}$:

$\vec{E} = -(-2\hat{i} - 3\hat{j} - 6\hat{k}) = 2\hat{i} + 3\hat{j} + 6\hat{k}$

The magnitude of the gravitational field intensity is:

$|\vec{E}| = \sqrt{2^{2} + 3^{2} + 6^{2}} = \sqrt{4 + 9 + 36} = \sqrt{49} = 7\text{ N/kg}$

Answer: $7\text{ N/kg}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two solid slabs, $P$ and $Q$, having the same cross-sectional area are placed in series to form a composite wall. The thickness of slab $P$ is twice the thickness of slab $Q$, and the thermal conductivity of slab $P$ is half the thermal conductivity of slab $Q$. In steady state, if the total temperature difference across the entire composite wall is $100^{\circ}\text{C}$, what is the temperature drop across slab $P$?
questions.solution:
Let the thickness of slab $Q$ be $x$ and its thermal conductivity be $k$.

The thickness of slab $P$ is $2x$ and its thermal conductivity is $\dfrac{k}{2}$.

The thermal resistance of a slab is given by $R = \dfrac{L}{kA}$.

For slab $Q$, $R_Q = \dfrac{x}{kA}$.

For slab $P$, $R_P = \dfrac{2x}{\left(\dfrac{k}{2}\right)A} = \dfrac{4x}{kA} = 4R_Q$.

In steady state, the heat current $H$ is the same through both slabs. The temperature drop across a slab is $\Delta T = H \cdot R$.

Therefore, $\Delta T_P = 4\Delta T_Q$.

Given the total temperature difference is $100^{\circ}\text{C}$:

$\Delta T_P + \Delta T_Q = 100^{\circ}\text{C}$

$\Delta T_P + \dfrac{\Delta T_P}{4} = 100^{\circ}\text{C}$

$\dfrac{5\Delta T_P}{4} = 100^{\circ}\text{C}$

$\Delta T_P = 80^{\circ}\text{C}$

Answer: $80^{\circ}\text{C}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A sealed container holds a gaseous mixture of Neon ($Ne$), Oxygen ($O_2$), and Carbon dioxide ($CO_2$) in thermal equilibrium at a constant temperature. Which of the following statements is correct regarding the root mean square (rms) speed of the molecules in this mixture?
options: The rms speed of $CO_2$ molecules is the greatest.
All molecules have the same rms speed because the mixture is in thermal equilibrium.
The rms speed of Neon molecules is the greatest.
The rms speed of Oxygen molecules is less than that of $CO_2$ molecules.
questions.solution:
The root mean square (rms) speed of gas molecules is given by the formula:

$v_{rms} = \sqrt{\dfrac{3RT}{M}}$

where $R$ is the universal gas constant, $T$ is the absolute temperature, and $M$ is the molar mass of the gas.

Since the gaseous mixture is in thermal equilibrium, the temperature $T$ is the same for all the gases. Therefore, the rms speed is inversely proportional to the square root of the molar mass:

$v_{rms} \propto \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{M}}$

The molar masses of the given gases are:
$M_{Ne} = 20 \text{ g/mol}$
$M_{O_2} = 32 \text{ g/mol}$
$M_{CO_2} = 44 \text{ g/mol}$

Comparing the molar masses:
$M_{Ne} \lt M_{O_2} \lt M_{CO_2}$

Consequently, the order of their rms speeds is:
$v_{rms}(Ne) \gt v_{rms}(O_2) \gt v_{rms}(CO_2)$

Thus, the rms speed of Neon molecules is the greatest.

Answer: The rms speed of Neon molecules is the greatest.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Four point charges $+Q$, $-2Q$, $+3Q$, and $-Q$ are fixed at the corners A, B, C, and D respectively of a square of side $a$, as shown in the figure. What is the work done by an external agent in bringing a test charge $q_0$ from infinity to the center O of the square? (where $\varepsilon_0$ is the permittivity of free space)
questions.solution:
The distance of the center $O$ from each corner of the square is $r = \dfrac{a}{\sqrt{2}}$.

The electric potential at the center $O$ due to the four point charges is the algebraic sum of the potentials due to each individual charge:

$V_O = \dfrac{1}{4 \pi \varepsilon_0} \left( \dfrac{Q_A}{r} + \dfrac{Q_B}{r} + \dfrac{Q_C}{r} + \dfrac{Q_D}{r} \right)$

Substituting the given values of the charges:

$V_O = \dfrac{1}{4 \pi \varepsilon_0 r} (Q - 2Q + 3Q - Q)$

$V_O = \dfrac{1}{4 \pi \varepsilon_0 r} (Q)$

Substituting $r = \dfrac{a}{\sqrt{2}}$:

$V_O = \dfrac{1}{4 \pi \varepsilon_0 \left(\dfrac{a}{\sqrt{2}}\right)} Q = \dfrac{\sqrt{2} Q}{4 \pi \varepsilon_0 a}$

The work done by an external agent in bringing a test charge $q_0$ from infinity to the center $O$ is given by:

$W = q_0 (V_O - V_{\infty})$

Since the potential at infinity is zero ($V_{\infty} = 0$):

$W = q_0 V_O = q_0 \left( \dfrac{\sqrt{2} Q}{4 \pi \varepsilon_0 a} \right) = \dfrac{\sqrt{2} Q q_0}{4 \pi \varepsilon_0 a}$

Answer: $\dfrac{\sqrt{2} Q q_0}{4 \pi \varepsilon_0 a}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
Two identical small dust particles, each of mass $3.0 \times 10^{-6} \text{ kg}$, are separated by a certain distance in free space. They are given identical charges $q$ such that the electrostatic repulsion between them is exactly $10^{12}$ times their gravitational attraction. What is the approximate value of the charge $q$ on each particle?
(Given: $G = 6.67 \times 10^{-11} \text{ N m}^2 \text{ kg}^{-2}$, $\dfrac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0} = 9 \times 10^9 \text{ N m}^2 \text{ C}^{-2}$)
questions.solution:
The electrostatic force of repulsion between the two particles is given by Coulomb's law:

$F_e = \dfrac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0} \dfrac{q^2}{r^2}$

The gravitational force of attraction between them is given by Newton's law of gravitation:

$F_g = G \dfrac{m^2}{r^2}$

Given that $F_e = 10^{12} F_g$, we have:

$\dfrac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0} \dfrac{q^2}{r^2} = 10^{12} G \dfrac{m^2}{r^2}$

Substituting the given values:

$9 \times 10^9 \times q^2 = 10^{12} \times 6.67 \times 10^{-11} \times (3.0 \times 10^{-6})^2$

$9 \times 10^9 \times q^2 = 10^{12} \times 6.67 \times 10^{-11} \times 9.0 \times 10^{-12}$

$9 \times 10^9 \times q^2 = 6.67 \times 9 \times 10^{-11}$

$q^2 = \dfrac{6.67 \times 9 \times 10^{-11}}{9 \times 10^9}$

$q^2 = 6.67 \times 10^{-20}$

Taking the square root on both sides:

$q = \sqrt{6.67} \times 10^{-10} \approx 2.58 \times 10^{-10} \text{ C}$

Rounding to the nearest given option, we get $q \approx 2.6 \times 10^{-10} \text{ C}$.

Answer: $2.6 \times 10^{-10} \text{ C}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A uniform resistance wire $MN$ of total resistance $R_0$ is connected across an ideal DC voltage source. A load resistor $R_L$ is connected between the end $M$ and a sliding contact $S$ on the wire. If the sliding contact is positioned such that the length $MS$ is two-thirds of the total length of the wire $MN$, what is the ratio of the potential difference across the load resistor $R_L$ to the potential difference across the remaining wire segment $SN$?
questions.solution:
Let the total resistance of the wire $MN$ be $R_0$.

Since the wire is uniform and the length $MS$ is two-thirds of the total length $MN$, the resistance of the segment $MS$ is:
$R_{MS} = \dfrac{2}{3} R_0$

The resistance of the remaining segment $SN$ is:
$R_{SN} = R_0 - \dfrac{2}{3} R_0 = \dfrac{1}{3} R_0$

The load resistor $R_L$ is connected in parallel with the segment $MS$. The equivalent resistance $R_{eq1}$ of this parallel combination is:
$R_{eq1} = \dfrac{R_L \cdot R_{MS}}{R_L + R_{MS}} = \dfrac{R_L \left(\dfrac{2}{3} R_0\right)}{R_L + \dfrac{2}{3} R_0} = \dfrac{2 R_L R_0}{3 R_L + 2 R_0}$

The segment $SN$ is in series with this parallel combination. In a series circuit, the potential difference across a component is proportional to its resistance. Therefore, the ratio of the potential difference across the load resistor $R_L$ (which is the same as the potential difference across the parallel combination, $V_{MS}$) to the potential difference across the segment $SN$ ($V_{SN}$) is equal to the ratio of their equivalent resistances:

$\dfrac{V_{MS}}{V_{SN}} = \dfrac{R_{eq1}}{R_{SN}}$

Substituting the values of $R_{eq1}$ and $R_{SN}$:
$\dfrac{V_{MS}}{V_{SN}} = \dfrac{\dfrac{2 R_L R_0}{3 R_L + 2 R_0}}{\dfrac{1}{3} R_0}$

$\dfrac{V_{MS}}{V_{SN}} = \dfrac{2 R_L R_0}{3 R_L + 2 R_0} \times \dfrac{3}{R_0} = \dfrac{6 R_L}{2 R_0 + 3 R_L}$

Answer: $\dfrac{6 R_L}{2 R_0 + 3 R_L}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
Two long, straight, parallel transmission cables, X and Y, are separated by a distance of $20 \text{ cm}$. Cable X carries a steady current of $20 \text{ A}$ and cable Y carries a steady current of $30 \text{ A}$ in the opposite direction. What is the magnitude and nature of the magnetic force per unit length experienced by cable Y?
(Take $\mu_0 = 4\pi \times 10^{-7} \text{ T m A}^{-1}$)
questions.solution:
The magnetic force per unit length between two long, straight, parallel current-carrying wires is given by the formula:

$\dfrac{F}{L} = \dfrac{\mu_0 I_1 I_2}{2\pi d}$

Given:
$I_1 = 20 \text{ A}$
$I_2 = 30 \text{ A}$
$d = 20 \text{ cm} = 0.2 \text{ m}$
$\mu_0 = 4\pi \times 10^{-7} \text{ T m A}^{-1}$

Substituting the values into the formula:

$\dfrac{F}{L} = \dfrac{4\pi \times 10^{-7} \times 20 \times 30}{2\pi \times 0.2}$

$\dfrac{F}{L} = \dfrac{2 \times 10^{-7} \times 600}{0.2}$

$\dfrac{F}{L} = \dfrac{1200 \times 10^{-7}}{0.2} = 6000 \times 10^{-7} = 6 \times 10^{-4} \text{ N m}^{-1}$

Since the currents in the two cables are flowing in opposite directions, the magnetic force between them is repulsive.

Answer: $6 \times 10^{-4} \text{ N m}^{-1}$, repulsive

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A tightly wound circular coil has $40$ turns, each of radius $10\text{ cm}$. If it carries a steady current of $4\text{ A}$, what is the magnitude of the magnetic field on its axis at a distance of $10\sqrt{3}\text{ cm}$ from the centre?
questions.solution:
The magnetic field on the axis of a circular coil is given by the formula:

$B = \dfrac{\mu_0 N I R^2}{2(R^2 + x^2)^{3/2}}$

Given values are:
$N = 40$
$R = 10\text{ cm} = 0.1\text{ m}$
$I = 4\text{ A}$
$x = 10\sqrt{3}\text{ cm} = 0.1\sqrt{3}\text{ m}$
$\mu_0 = 4\pi \times 10^{-7}\text{ T}\cdot\text{m/A}$

First, calculate the term $(R^2 + x^2)$:
$R^2 + x^2 = (0.1)^2 + (0.1\sqrt{3})^2 = 0.01 + 0.03 = 0.04\text{ m}^2$

Now, calculate $(R^2 + x^2)^{3/2}$:
$(0.04)^{3/2} = (0.2^2)^{3/2} = (0.2)^3 = 0.008\text{ m}^3$

Substituting these values into the formula for $B$:
$B = \dfrac{4\pi \times 10^{-7} \times 40 \times 4 \times (0.1)^2}{2 \times 0.008}$

$B = \dfrac{4\pi \times 10^{-7} \times 1.6}{0.016}$

$B = 4\pi \times 10^{-7} \times 100$

$B = 4\pi \times 10^{-5}\text{ T}$

Answer: $4\pi \times 10^{-5}\text{ T}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The magnetic flux passing through a stationary square coil is given by the expression $\phi = 2t^3 - 3t^2 - 12t + 8 \text{ Wb}$, where $t$ is the time in seconds. At what time will the induced electromotive force (emf) in the coil be zero?
questions.solution:
The magnetic flux is given by $\phi = 2t^3 - 3t^2 - 12t + 8$

According to Faraday's law of electromagnetic induction, the induced emf is given by $e = -\dfrac{d\phi}{dt}$

Differentiating the given expression with respect to time $t$

$e = -\dfrac{d}{dt}(2t^3 - 3t^2 - 12t + 8)$

$e = -(6t^2 - 6t - 12)$

For the induced emf to be zero, $e = 0$

$6t^2 - 6t - 12 = 0$

$t^2 - t - 2 = 0$

$(t - 2)(t + 1) = 0$

Since time cannot be negative, $t = 2 \text{ s}$

Answer: $2 \text{ s}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
An amateur astronomer constructs an astronomical refracting telescope using two convex lenses of focal lengths $100 \text{ cm}$ and $4 \text{ cm}$. The telescope is used to observe the moon in normal adjustment. Consider the following statements regarding this telescope:
(I) The distance between the objective lens and the eyepiece is $1.04 \text{ m}$.
(II) The magnification of the telescope is $+25$.
(III) The final image of the moon formed by the telescope is virtual and inverted.
(IV) The objective lens has a larger aperture than the eyepiece to gather more light.

The correct statements are:
questions.solution:
For an astronomical telescope in normal adjustment, the distance between the objective lens and the eyepiece (tube length) is given by $L = f_o + f_e$.

Given $f_o = 100 \text{ cm}$ and $f_e = 4 \text{ cm}$, we have $L = 100 + 4 = 104 \text{ cm} = 1.04 \text{ m}$. Thus, statement (I) is correct.

The magnifying power of the telescope in normal adjustment is $m = -\dfrac{f_o}{f_e} = -\dfrac{100}{4} = -25$. The negative sign indicates that the final image is inverted. Statement (II) claims the magnification is $+25$, which is incorrect.

In an astronomical telescope, the objective lens forms a real, inverted intermediate image. The eyepiece acts as a simple magnifier, forming a virtual image of this intermediate image. Therefore, the final image is virtual and inverted with respect to the original object. Thus, statement (III) is correct.

The objective lens is designed with a larger aperture to gather more light from distant, faint objects, which increases the brightness of the image and improves the resolving power of the telescope. Thus, statement (IV) is correct.

Therefore, the correct statements are (I), (III), and (IV).

Answer: (I), (III) and (IV)

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
In the given digital logic circuit, two inputs, $A$ and $B$, are passed through two separate NAND gates where both inputs of each respective gate are shorted together. The outputs from these two NAND gates are then fed as the two inputs into a third NAND gate to produce the final output $Y$.

Which of the following basic logic gates does this entire circuit arrangement represent?
questions.solution:
The first NAND gate has both its inputs connected to $A$. Its output acts as a NOT gate, giving $\overline{A \cdot A} = \overline{A}$.

The second NAND gate has both its inputs connected to $B$. Its output acts as a NOT gate, giving $\overline{B \cdot B} = \overline{B}$.

These two outputs are fed into a third NAND gate. The final output $Y$ is given by:

$Y = \overline{\overline{A} \cdot \overline{B}}$

Using De Morgan's theorem, $\overline{X \cdot Y} = \overline{X} + \overline{Y}$:

$Y = \overline{\overline{A}} + \overline{\overline{B}}$

$Y = A + B$

This is the Boolean expression for an OR gate.

Answer: OR gate

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A chemist determines the concentration of an aqueous solution to be $0.224 \text{ mol L}^{-1}$. If a measured volume of $3.4 \text{ L}$ of this solution is transferred to a reaction flask, what is the number of moles of the solute present, reported to the correct number of significant figures?
questions.solution:
The number of moles of solute is calculated by multiplying the concentration by the volume.

$n = C \times V$

$n = 0.224 \text{ mol L}^{-1} \times 3.4 \text{ L} = 0.7616 \text{ mol}$

The concentration $0.224 \text{ mol L}^{-1}$ has three significant figures, and the volume $3.4 \text{ L}$ has two significant figures. In multiplication, the final result must be reported to the least number of significant figures present in the measured quantities, which is two.

Rounding $0.7616 \text{ mol}$ to two significant figures gives $0.76 \text{ mol}$.

Answer: $0.76 \text{ mol}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Observe the given figure showing the boundary surface diagrams of four different atomic orbitals labeled P, Q, R, and S.

Match the orbital shapes in List I with their corresponding designations and azimuthal quantum numbers in List II.

List IList II
AShape P1$p_x$ orbital, $l = 1$
BShape Q2$d_{z^2}$ orbital, $l = 2$
CShape R3$s$ orbital, $l = 0$
DShape S4$d_{xz}$ orbital, $l = 2$

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
Shape P is spherically symmetric, which corresponds to an $s$ orbital. For an $s$ orbital, the azimuthal quantum number is $l = 0$. Thus, A matches with 3.

Shape Q has two lobes oriented along the x-axis, which corresponds to a $p_x$ orbital. For a $p$ orbital, $l = 1$. Thus, B matches with 1.

Shape R has four lobes lying in the xz plane between the x and z axes, which corresponds to a $d_{xz}$ orbital. For a $d$ orbital, $l = 2$. Thus, C matches with 4.

Shape S has two lobes along the z-axis and a donut-shaped ring in the xy plane, which corresponds to a $d_{z^2}$ orbital. For a $d$ orbital, $l = 2$. Thus, D matches with 2.

The correct matching is (A)-(3), (B)-(1), (C)-(4), (D)-(2).

Answer: (A)-(3), (B)-(1), (C)-(4), (D)-(2)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
The successive ionization enthalpies (in $\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$) of an element 'M' are given below:
$IE_1 = 577$
$IE_2 = 1816$
$IE_3 = 2744$
$IE_4 = 11577$
$IE_5 = 14842$

Based on this data, what will be the formula of the most stable oxide formed by element M?
questions.solution:
The successive ionization enthalpies of element M are given as:
$IE_1 = 577 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$
$IE_2 = 1816 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$
$IE_3 = 2744 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$
$IE_4 = 11577 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$
$IE_5 = 14842 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$

There is a sudden large jump in the ionization enthalpy between $IE_3$ and $IE_4$. This indicates that the removal of the fourth electron requires a very high amount of energy, which means the fourth electron is being removed from a stable noble gas core.

Thus, element M has 3 valence electrons and its most stable oxidation state is $+3$.

The formula of the oxide formed by an element in the $+3$ oxidation state is $M_2O_3$.

Answer: $M_{2}O_{3}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Based on VSEPR theory, which of the following sequences correctly represents the increasing order of bond angles for the given molecules?
questions.solution:
In $\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{S}$, the central atom sulfur is $sp^3$ hybridized and has two lone pairs. Due to strong lone pair-lone pair repulsions, the bond angle decreases significantly to approximately $92^\circ$.

In $\mathrm{CH}_4$, the central atom carbon is $sp^3$ hybridized with no lone pairs. The geometry is perfectly tetrahedral with a bond angle of $109.5^\circ$.

In $\mathrm{BF}_3$, the central atom boron is $sp^2$ hybridized with no lone pairs. The geometry is trigonal planar with a bond angle of $120^\circ$.

In $\mathrm{BeF}_2$, the central atom beryllium is $sp$ hybridized with no lone pairs. The geometry is linear with a bond angle of $180^\circ$.

Therefore, the increasing order of bond angles is $\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{S} \lt \mathrm{CH}_4 \lt \mathrm{BF}_3 \lt \mathrm{BeF}_2$.

Answer: $\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{S} \lt \mathrm{CH}_4 \lt \mathrm{BF}_3 \lt \mathrm{BeF}_2$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Match List I (Molecule/Ion) with List II (Shape) :

List IList II
A$\mathrm{SF}_4$1Square planar
B$\mathrm{XeF}_4$2Linear
C$\mathrm{I}_3^-$3Bent
D$\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}$4See-saw

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
For $\mathrm{SF}_4$, the central atom $\mathrm{S}$ has $6$ valence electrons. It forms $4$ bond pairs and has $1$ lone pair. The hybridization is $sp^3d$ and the shape is see-saw.

For $\mathrm{XeF}_4$, the central atom $\mathrm{Xe}$ has $8$ valence electrons. It forms $4$ bond pairs and has $2$ lone pairs. The hybridization is $sp^3d^2$ and the shape is square planar.

For $\mathrm{I}_3^-$, the central atom $\mathrm{I}$ has $7$ valence electrons plus $1$ from the negative charge, giving $8$ electrons. It forms $2$ bond pairs and has $3$ lone pairs. The hybridization is $sp^3d$ and the shape is linear.

For $\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}$, the central atom $\mathrm{O}$ has $6$ valence electrons. It forms $2$ bond pairs and has $2$ lone pairs. The hybridization is $sp^3$ and the shape is bent.

Thus, the correct matching is A-4, B-1, C-2, D-3.

Answer: A-4, B-1, C-2, D-3

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
What is the hybridization of the $\mathrm{C}_2$ and $\mathrm{C}_4$ carbon atoms, respectively, in the given compound?
$\mathrm{CH}_3-\mathrm{C}(=\mathrm{O})-\mathrm{CH}_2-\mathrm{C} \equiv \mathrm{CH}$
questions.solution:
According to IUPAC nomenclature rules, the principal functional group determines the numbering of the carbon chain. The ketone group ($ \gt C=O$) has a higher priority than the alkyne group ($-C \equiv C-$).

Numbering the chain to give the ketone the lowest possible locant, we start from left to right:
$C_1$: $\mathrm{CH}_3$
$C_2$: $\mathrm{C}(=\mathrm{O})$
$C_3$: $\mathrm{CH}_2$
$C_4$: $\mathrm{C}$
$C_5$: $\mathrm{CH}$

The $C_2$ atom is bonded to three atoms (one oxygen and two carbons) with no lone pairs, forming $3\sigma$ bonds and $1\pi$ bond. Therefore, its hybridization is $sp^2$.

The $C_4$ atom is bonded to two atoms (two carbons) with no lone pairs, forming $2\sigma$ bonds and $2\pi$ bonds. Therefore, its hybridization is $sp$.

Thus, the hybridization of $C_2$ and $C_4$ are $sp^2$ and $sp$, respectively.

Answer: $sp^2$ and $sp$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
London dispersion forces are the primary intermolecular forces present in non-polar molecules. Arrange the following hydrocarbons in the increasing order of the magnitude of London dispersion forces between their molecules:

(a) 2,2-Dimethylbutane
(b) n-Butane
(c) n-Hexane
(d) 2-Methylpropane
(e) n-Pentane

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
London dispersion forces depend on the molecular mass and the surface area of the molecules. The magnitude of these forces increases with an increase in molecular mass due to higher polarizability.

The molecular formulas of the given hydrocarbons are:
(a) 2,2-Dimethylbutane: $C_6H_{14}$
(b) n-Butane: $C_4H_{10}$
(c) n-Hexane: $C_6H_{14}$
(d) 2-Methylpropane: $C_4H_{10}$
(e) n-Pentane: $C_5H_{12}$

Based on molecular mass, the general order of dispersion forces is $C_4H_{10} \lt C_5H_{12} \lt C_6H_{14}$.

For isomers having the same molecular mass, branching decreases the surface area of the molecule, which weakens the London dispersion forces.

Comparing the $C_4H_{10}$ isomers, 2-methylpropane is branched while n-butane is a straight chain. Thus, the forces are weaker in 2-methylpropane: (d) $\lt $ (b).

Comparing the $C_6H_{14}$ isomers, 2,2-dimethylbutane is highly branched while n-hexane is a straight chain. Thus, the forces are weaker in 2,2-dimethylbutane: (a) $\lt $ (c).

Combining these observations, the increasing order of the magnitude of London dispersion forces is (d) $\lt $ (b) $\lt $ (e) $\lt $ (a) $\lt $ (c).

Answer: (d) $\lt $ (b) $\lt $ (e) $\lt $ (a) $\lt $ (c)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the total number of bonding electrons present in a nitrogen ($\mathrm{N}_2$) molecule?
questions.solution:
The total number of electrons in a nitrogen molecule ($\mathrm{N}_2$) is $14$.

The molecular orbital electronic configuration of $\mathrm{N}_2$ is:
$\sigma_{1s}^{2} \sigma^{*}_{1s}^{2} \sigma_{2s}^{2} \sigma^{*}_{2s}^{2} \pi_{2p_x}^{2} \pi_{2p_y}^{2} \sigma_{2p_z}^{2}$

The bonding molecular orbitals are $\sigma_{1s}$, $\sigma_{2s}$, $\pi_{2p_x}$, $\pi_{2p_y}$, and $\sigma_{2p_z}$.

Total number of bonding electrons = $2 + 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 = 10$.

Answer: $10$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
During a reversible isothermal compression, $0.5 \mathrm{~mol}$ of an ideal gas at $400 \mathrm{~K}$ is compressed from a pressure of $2 \mathrm{~atm}$ to $10 \mathrm{~atm}$. What is the change in internal energy ($\Delta U$) for the gas?
(Given: $\mathrm{R} = 8.314 \mathrm{~J} \mathrm{~K}^{-1} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}$, $\log 5 = 0.699$)
questions.solution:
For an ideal gas, the internal energy depends only on its temperature.

In an isothermal process, the temperature of the system remains constant, which means $\Delta T = 0$.

The change in internal energy is given by the relation $\Delta U = n C_v \Delta T$.

Since $\Delta T = 0$, it follows that $\Delta U = 0 \mathrm{~J}$.

Answer: $0 \mathrm{~J}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: An aqueous solution of a weak monoprotic acid, $\mathrm{HA}$, has a concentration of $0.02 \mathrm{~M}$. If the acid is $0.05\%$ dissociated at $298 \mathrm{~K}$, the $\mathrm{pH}$ of the solution is :
questions.solution:
Given concentration of the weak monoprotic acid, $C = 0.02 \mathrm{~M}$

Degree of dissociation, $\alpha = 0.05\% = \dfrac{0.05}{100} = 5 \times 10^{-4}$

For a weak monoprotic acid, the concentration of hydrogen ions is given by:

$[H^+] = C\alpha$

Substituting the given values:

$[H^+] = 0.02 \times 5 \times 10^{-4} = 10^{-5} \mathrm{~M}$

The $\mathrm{pH}$ of the solution is calculated as:

$\mathrm{pH} = -\log[H^+]$

$\mathrm{pH} = -\log(10^{-5}) = 5$

Answer: 5

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Consider the $\mathrm{Fe}^{3+}$ ion in its ground state. Which of the following statements regarding its electronic configuration is INCORRECT?
options: The total number of occupied subshells is $6$.
There are exactly $9$ completely filled atomic orbitals.
Electrons are distributed across $4$ principal quantum shells.
The number of unpaired electrons present is $5$.
questions.solution:
The atomic number of $\mathrm{Fe}$ is $26$.

The electronic configuration of the $\mathrm{Fe}$ atom is $1s^{2} 2s^{2} 2p^{6} 3s^{2} 3p^{6} 4s^{2} 3d^{6}$.

To form the $\mathrm{Fe}^{3+}$ ion, three electrons are removed (two from the $4s$ subshell and one from the $3d$ subshell).

The electronic configuration of $\mathrm{Fe}^{3+}$ is $1s^{2} 2s^{2} 2p^{6} 3s^{2} 3p^{6} 3d^{5}$.

Evaluating the given options:

The occupied subshells are $1s, 2s, 2p, 3s, 3p,$ and $3d$. The total number of occupied subshells is $6$.

The completely filled atomic orbitals are one in $1s$, one in $2s$, three in $2p$, one in $3s$, and three in $3p$. The total number of completely filled orbitals is $1 + 1 + 3 + 1 + 3 = 9$.

The electrons are present in the principal quantum shells $n=1, n=2,$ and $n=3$. The $n=4$ shell is empty. Thus, electrons are distributed across $3$ principal quantum shells, not $4$.

The $3d^{5}$ configuration has $5$ unpaired electrons according to Hund's rule.

Therefore, the statement regarding the $4$ principal quantum shells is incorrect.

Answer: Electrons are distributed across $4$ principal quantum shells.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
The given compound is to be reduced to its corresponding primary amine.

Which of the following reagent mixtures is preferred for this conversion in industrial processes because the acid is regenerated during the reaction?
options: $\mathrm{H_2}$ gas in the presence of finely divided $\mathrm{Ni}$
questions.solution:
Reduction of nitro compounds to primary amines can be carried out using metal-acid mixtures such as $\mathrm{Sn}/\mathrm{HCl}$ or $\mathrm{Fe}/\mathrm{HCl}$.

In industrial processes, the use of iron scrap ($\mathrm{Fe}$) and hydrochloric acid ($\mathrm{HCl}$) is preferred over $\mathrm{Sn}/\mathrm{HCl}$.

This is because the $\mathrm{FeCl_2}$ formed during the reaction gets hydrolysed to release hydrochloric acid back into the reaction mixture:
$\mathrm{FeCl_2} + 2\mathrm{H_2O} \rightarrow \mathrm{Fe(OH)_2} + 2\mathrm{HCl}$

Thus, only a small amount of $\mathrm{HCl}$ is required to initiate the reaction, making the process highly cost-effective.

Answer: $\mathrm{Fe}$ scrap and $\mathrm{HCl}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
At a given temperature and a constant partial pressure, the mole fractions of four gases $\mathrm{P}$, $\mathrm{Q}$, $\mathrm{R}$, and $\mathrm{S}$ dissolved in a solvent are $2 \times 10^{-3}$, $5 \times 10^{-4}$, $1 \times 10^{-2}$, and $8 \times 10^{-5}$ respectively.

The correct increasing order of their Henry's law constants ($\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{H}}$) is :
questions.solution:
According to Henry's law, the partial pressure of a gas over a solution is given by $p = K_H x$, where $K_H$ is Henry's law constant and $x$ is the mole fraction of the gas in the solution.

At a constant partial pressure, $K_H$ is inversely proportional to the mole fraction $x$, i.e., $K_H \propto \dfrac{1}{x}$.

The given mole fractions are:
$x_P = 2 \times 10^{-3}$
$x_Q = 5 \times 10^{-4} = 0.5 \times 10^{-3}$
$x_R = 1 \times 10^{-2} = 10 \times 10^{-3}$
$x_S = 8 \times 10^{-5} = 0.08 \times 10^{-3}$

The increasing order of mole fractions is $x_S \lt x_Q \lt x_P \lt x_R$.

Therefore, the increasing order of Henry's law constants is the reverse of the mole fraction order:
$\mathrm{R} \lt \mathrm{P} \lt \mathrm{Q} \lt \mathrm{S}$

Answer: $\mathrm{R} \lt \mathrm{P} \lt \mathrm{Q} \lt \mathrm{S}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the oxidation number of $\mathrm{Mn}$ in $\mathrm{K_2MnO_4}$?
questions.solution:
Let the oxidation number of $\mathrm{Mn}$ in $\mathrm{K_2MnO_4}$ be $x$.

The oxidation number of potassium ($\mathrm{K}$) is $+1$ and that of oxygen ($\mathrm{O}$) is $-2$.

Since the sum of oxidation numbers of all atoms in a neutral molecule is zero, we have:

$2(+1) + x + 4(-2) = 0$

$2 + x - 8 = 0$

$x - 6 = 0$

$x = +6$

The oxidation number of $\mathrm{Mn}$ in $\mathrm{K_2MnO_4}$ is $+6$.

Answer: $+6$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
The standard reduction potential ($E^\circ$) of the $F_2/F^-$ electrode is the highest among all halogens, making $F_2$ the most powerful oxidizing agent. Which of the following thermodynamic factors primarily account for this exceptionally high $E^\circ$ value?

(I) Highly negative hydration enthalpy of the $F^-$ ion.
(II) Lower bond dissociation enthalpy of the $F_2$ molecule compared to $Cl_2$.
(III) More negative electron gain enthalpy of the $F$ atom compared to $Cl$.
(IV) Absence of d-orbitals in the valence shell of fluorine.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
The standard reduction potential ($E^{\circ}$) of a halogen is determined by the overall enthalpy change of the following three steps:

1. Dissociation of the halogen molecule into atoms: $\dfrac{1}{2} X_2(g) \rightarrow X(g)$ (Bond dissociation enthalpy, $\Delta_{diss}H^{\circ}$)
2. Addition of an electron to the atom: $X(g) + e^- \rightarrow X^-(g)$ (Electron gain enthalpy, $\Delta_{eg}H^{\circ}$)
3. Hydration of the gaseous ion: $X^-(g) + aq \rightarrow X^-(aq)$ (Hydration enthalpy, $\Delta_{hyd}H^{\circ}$)

For fluorine, the bond dissociation enthalpy of $F_2$ is lower than that of $Cl_2$ due to strong interelectronic repulsions between the lone pairs on the small $F$ atoms. This makes the dissociation step less endothermic.

The hydration enthalpy of the $F^-$ ion is highly negative because of its small size and high charge density. This highly exothermic step is the primary driving force for the high $E^{\circ}$ value.

The electron gain enthalpy of $F$ is actually less negative than that of $Cl$, so statement (III) is incorrect. The absence of d-orbitals (IV) is a structural fact but not a thermodynamic factor in this cycle.

Therefore, the exceptionally high $E^{\circ}$ value of the $F_2/F^-$ electrode is primarily due to the highly negative hydration enthalpy of $F^-$ and the lower bond dissociation enthalpy of $F_2$.

Answer: (I) and (II) only

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: While moving along the inner transition elements, the element-to-element decrease in the ionic radii of $M^{3+}$ ions is observed to be more significant in the actinoid series compared to the lanthanoid series. Which of the following statements correctly explains this observation?
options: The $5f$ electrons shield the increasing nuclear charge less effectively than the $4f$ electrons.
The $5f$ orbitals are more deeply buried in the atomic core than the $4f$ orbitals.
The $4f$ electrons exhibit a weaker penetration effect towards the nucleus than the $5f$ electrons.
The energy gap between $5f$ and $6d$ orbitals is much larger than that between $4f$ and $5d$ orbitals.
questions.solution:
The decrease in ionic radii across the actinoid series (actinoid contraction) is more significant from element to element than the corresponding decrease in the lanthanoid series (lanthanoid contraction).

This occurs because the $5f$ orbitals are more diffuse and extend further from the nucleus compared to the $4f$ orbitals. As a result, the $5f$ electrons shield the increasing nuclear charge less effectively than the $4f$ electrons.

Due to this poorer shielding by $5f$ electrons, the effective nuclear charge experienced by the outermost electrons increases more rapidly across the actinoid series, leading to a greater contraction in size.

Answer: The $5f$ electrons shield the increasing nuclear charge less effectively than the $4f$ electrons.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Predict the correct order of reactivity of the following four primary bromides towards $\mathrm{S}_{\mathrm{N}}2$ reaction.
(I) $\mathrm{CH}_3\mathrm{CH}_2\mathrm{CH}(\mathrm{CH}_3)\mathrm{CH}_2\mathrm{Br}$
(II) $\left(\mathrm{CH}_3\right)_3\mathrm{CCH}_2\mathrm{Br}$
(III) $\mathrm{CH}_3\mathrm{CH}_2\mathrm{CH}_2\mathrm{CH}_2\mathrm{Br}$
(IV) $\mathrm{CH}_3\mathrm{CH}\left(\mathrm{CH}_3\right)\mathrm{CH}_2\mathrm{CH}_2\mathrm{Br}$
questions.solution:
The rate of an $\mathrm{S}_{\mathrm{N}}2$ reaction is inversely proportional to the steric hindrance around the electrophilic carbon atom. Since all the given compounds are primary alkyl bromides, we must compare the steric hindrance caused by branching at the $\beta$ and $\gamma$ positions.

(III) $\mathrm{CH}_3\mathrm{CH}_2\mathrm{CH}_2\mathrm{CH}_2\mathrm{Br}$ is a straight-chain primary bromide with no branching, offering the least steric hindrance.

(IV) $\mathrm{CH}_3\mathrm{CH}(\mathrm{CH}_3)\mathrm{CH}_2\mathrm{CH}_2\mathrm{Br}$ has branching at the $\gamma$-carbon, which introduces slight steric hindrance compared to the unbranched chain.

(I) $\mathrm{CH}_3\mathrm{CH}_2\mathrm{CH}(\mathrm{CH}_3)\mathrm{CH}_2\mathrm{Br}$ has branching at the $\beta$-carbon (a tertiary $\beta$-carbon), which significantly increases steric hindrance to the approaching nucleophile.

(II) $(\mathrm{CH}_3)_3\mathrm{CCH}_2\mathrm{Br}$ (neopentyl bromide) has a quaternary $\beta$-carbon, providing maximum steric hindrance and making it practically unreactive towards $\mathrm{S}_{\mathrm{N}}2$ reactions.

Therefore, the steric hindrance increases in the order (III) $\lt $ (IV) $\lt $ (I) $\lt $ (II).

The reactivity towards $\mathrm{S}_{\mathrm{N}}2$ follows the reverse order: (III) $ \gt $ (IV) $ \gt $ (I) $ \gt $ (II).

Answer: (III) $ \gt $ (IV) $ \gt $ (I) $ \gt $ (II)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Carbonyl compounds undergo a variety of nucleophilic reactions. Which of the following derivatives of cyclohexanone is formed strictly via a nucleophilic addition mechanism, without any subsequent elimination of a small molecule like water?
questions.solution:
The formation of cyclohexanone cyanohydrin involves the reaction of cyclohexanone with hydrogen cyanide (HCN). The cyanide ion ($CN^-$) acts as a nucleophile and attacks the electrophilic carbonyl carbon, forming a tetrahedral alkoxide intermediate. This intermediate is then protonated to yield the cyanohydrin. The entire process is a pure nucleophilic addition reaction, and no small molecule like water is eliminated.

In contrast, the formation of cyclohexanone oxime (from hydroxylamine), cyclohexanone semicarbazone (from semicarbazide), and cyclohexanone ethylene ketal (from ethylene glycol) all proceed via an initial nucleophilic addition followed by the elimination of a water molecule (nucleophilic addition-elimination mechanism).

Answer: Cyclohexanone cyanohydrin

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: An organic compound, 2,3-dichlorobutane, exhibits stereoisomerism due to the presence of chiral carbon atoms. What is the number of optically active isomers and meso forms possible for this compound, respectively?
questions.solution:
The given compound is 2,3-dichlorobutane, whose structure is $CH_3-CH(Cl)-CH(Cl)-CH_3$.

It contains two similar chiral carbon atoms ($n = 2$). Since the molecule can be divided into two equal halves, it is symmetrical.

For a symmetrical molecule with an even number of chiral centers ($n$), the number of optically active isomers is given by $a = 2^{n-1}$.

Substituting $n = 2$, we get $a = 2^{2-1} = 2$.

The number of meso forms is given by $m = 2^{\dfrac{n}{2}-1}$.

Substituting $n = 2$, we get $m = 2^{\dfrac{2}{2}-1} = 2^0 = 1$.

Thus, there are 2 optically active isomers (a pair of enantiomers) and 1 meso form.

Answer: 2 and 1

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: When milk is converted into curd, the proteins present in it undergo denaturation due to the decrease in pH caused by lactic acid. Which of the following correctly describes the structural changes occurring in the protein during this process?
options: The primary structure is destroyed while the secondary and tertiary structures remain intact.
The secondary and tertiary structures are destroyed, but the primary structure remains intact.
The peptide bonds are cleaved, breaking the protein chain into free amino acids.
The protein chain undergoes further coiling to form a more complex quaternary structure.
questions.solution:
During the conversion of milk into curd, the lactic acid produced by bacteria lowers the pH, leading to the denaturation of milk proteins (such as casein).

Denaturation is a process in which proteins lose their secondary and tertiary structures due to the disruption of non-covalent interactions (like hydrogen bonds, hydrophobic interactions, and disulfide bridges) caused by changes in temperature, pH, or chemical environment.

However, the primary structure, which consists of the sequence of amino acids held together by strong covalent peptide bonds, remains intact and is not destroyed during denaturation.

Answer: The secondary and tertiary structures are destroyed, but the primary structure remains intact.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
The minimum energy required to eject an electron from the surface of a specific metal is $4.15 \times 10^5 \text{ J mol}^{-1}$. If the metal surface is exposed to electromagnetic radiation of wavelength $200 \text{ nm}$, what will be the maximum kinetic energy of the emitted photoelectrons per mole?

$\left(h = 6.626 \times 10^{-34} \text{ Js}, c = 3 \times 10^8 \text{ ms}^{-1}, N_A = 6.022 \times 10^{23} \text{ mol}^{-1}\right)$
questions.solution:
The energy of one mole of incident photons is given by $E = \dfrac{hcN_A}{\lambda}$

Substituting the given values:

$E = \dfrac{6.626 \times 10^{-34} \times 3 \times 10^8 \times 6.022 \times 10^{23}}{200 \times 10^{-9}}$

$E = \dfrac{19.878 \times 10^{-26} \times 6.022 \times 10^{23}}{2 \times 10^{-7}}$

$E = 9.939 \times 10^{-19} \times 6.022 \times 10^{23}$

$E = 59.85 \times 10^4 \text{ J mol}^{-1} = 5.985 \times 10^5 \text{ J mol}^{-1}$

According to Einstein's photoelectric equation, the maximum kinetic energy is:

$K_{\text{max}} = E - W$

$K_{\text{max}} = 5.985 \times 10^5 - 4.15 \times 10^5$

$K_{\text{max}} = 1.835 \times 10^5 \text{ J mol}^{-1}$

Rounding off to three significant figures, we get $1.84 \times 10^5 \text{ J mol}^{-1}$.

Answer: $1.84 \times 10^5 \text{ J mol}^{-1}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
For the reaction given below, the equilibrium constant $K_c$ is $8.3 \times 10^3$ at $500 \mathrm{~K}$.

$2\mathrm{Na}_2\mathrm{O}_2(\mathrm{s}) + 2\mathrm{CO}_2(\mathrm{g}) \rightleftharpoons 2\mathrm{Na}_2\mathrm{CO}_3(\mathrm{s}) + \mathrm{O}_2(\mathrm{g})$

What is the value of $K_p$ for this reaction at the same temperature?
(Given: $R = 0.083 \mathrm{~L~bar~K^{-1}~mol^{-1}}$)
questions.solution:
The given reaction is $2\mathrm{Na}_2\mathrm{O}_2(\mathrm{s}) + 2\mathrm{CO}_2(\mathrm{g}) \rightleftharpoons 2\mathrm{Na}_2\mathrm{CO}_3(\mathrm{s}) + \mathrm{O}_2(\mathrm{g})$

The change in the number of moles of gaseous species is $\Delta n_g = n_p - n_r = 1 - 2 = -1$

The relationship between $K_p$ and $K_c$ is given by $K_p = K_c(RT)^{\Delta n_g}$

Substituting the given values:

$K_p = 8.3 \times 10^3 \times (0.083 \times 500)^{-1}$

$K_p = \dfrac{8.3 \times 10^3}{41.5}$

$K_p = 200 = 2.0 \times 10^2$

Answer: $2.0 \times 10^2$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: If the overall stability constant ($\beta_2$) for the formation of the $\left[\mathrm{Ag}(\mathrm{CN})_2\right]^-$ complex is $5.0 \times 10^{18}$, determine the overall dissociation equilibrium constant (instability constant) for this complex ion.
questions.solution:
The overall dissociation equilibrium constant (instability constant) is the reciprocal of the overall stability constant ($\beta_2$).

$K_d = \dfrac{1}{\beta_2}$

Substituting the given value:

$K_d = \dfrac{1}{5.0 \times 10^{18}}$

$K_d = 0.2 \times 10^{-18}$

$K_d = 2.0 \times 10^{-19}$

Answer: $2.0 \times 10^{-19}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Consider the given molecule with four labeled $\text{C}-\text{Cl}$ bonds (P, Q, R, and S).

Which of these bonds will undergo heterolytic cleavage most readily to form a carbocation?
questions.solution:
The ease of heterolytic cleavage of a $\text{C}-\text{Cl}$ bond depends on the stability of the carbocation formed after the departure of the chloride ion ($\text{Cl}^-$). The more stable the carbocation, the more readily the bond will cleave.

Let us analyze the carbocations formed by the cleavage of each labeled bond:

1. Bond P: Cleavage forms a tertiary benzylic carbocation. This carbocation is highly stabilized by resonance with the benzene ring and by hyperconjugation from the six $\alpha$-hydrogens of the two methyl groups.

2. Bond Q: Cleavage forms a primary benzylic carbocation. It is stabilized by resonance with the benzene ring, but it is less stable than the tertiary benzylic carbocation formed from P.

3. Bond R: Cleavage forms a phenyl cation. This is highly unstable because the positive charge resides in an $sp^2$ hybridized orbital that is perpendicular to the $\pi$-system of the benzene ring, meaning it cannot be stabilized by resonance. Furthermore, the $\text{C}-\text{Cl}$ bond here has partial double bond character due to resonance, making it difficult to break.

4. Bond S: Cleavage forms a primary alkyl carbocation ($\text{-CH}_2\text{-CH}_2^+$). This carbocation lacks resonance stabilization and is relatively unstable.

Comparing the stabilities of the resulting carbocations, the order is:
Tertiary benzylic (from P) > Primary benzylic (from Q) > Primary alkyl (from S) > Phenyl (from R).

Since the carbocation formed from the cleavage of bond P is the most stable, bond P will undergo heterolytic cleavage most readily.

Answer: Bond P

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
An inorganic reaction sequence involving potassium dichromate is shown in the given flowchart.

Identify the chemical formula of the reddish-brown gas (X), the yellow precipitate (Z), and the oxidation state of the transition metal in gas (X).
questions.solution:
The given reaction sequence is the chromyl chloride test for chloride ions.

Reaction 1: Heating $\text{K}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7$ with $\text{NaCl}$ and conc. $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ produces reddish-brown vapors of chromyl chloride.

$\text{K}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7 + 4\text{NaCl} + 6\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4 \rightarrow 2\text{KHSO}_4 + 4\text{NaHSO}_4 + 2\text{CrO}_2\text{Cl}_2 + 3\text{H}_2\text{O}$

Gas (X) is $\text{CrO}_2\text{Cl}_2$.

Reaction 2: Passing $\text{CrO}_2\text{Cl}_2$ gas into aqueous $\text{NaOH}$ gives a yellow solution of sodium chromate.

$\text{CrO}_2\text{Cl}_2 + 4\text{NaOH} \rightarrow \text{Na}_2\text{CrO}_4 + 2\text{NaCl} + 2\text{H}_2\text{O}$

Solution (Y) contains $\text{Na}_2\text{CrO}_4$.

Reaction 3: Adding lead acetate to the yellow solution forms a yellow precipitate of lead chromate.

$\text{Na}_2\text{CrO}_4 + (\text{CH}_3\text{COO})_2\text{Pb} \rightarrow \text{PbCrO}_4 + 2\text{CH}_3\text{COONa}$

Precipitate (Z) is $\text{PbCrO}_4$.

Oxidation state of Cr in $\text{CrO}_2\text{Cl}_2$:
Let the oxidation state of Cr be $x$.
$x + 2(-2) + 2(-1) = 0 \Rightarrow x = +6$

Answer: X = $\text{CrO}_2\text{Cl}_2$, Z = $\text{PbCrO}_4$, Oxidation state = +6

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Consider the following electrochemical cell reaction:
$\mathrm{Cr}(\mathrm{s}) + 3\mathrm{Ag}^{+}(\mathrm{aq}) \longrightarrow \mathrm{Cr}^{3+}(\mathrm{aq}) + 3\mathrm{Ag}(\mathrm{s})$
If the standard cell potential ($E^{\circ}_{\text{cell}}$) is $1.54 \text{ V}$, determine the standard Gibbs free energy change ($\Delta G^{\circ}$) for the process.
(Given: $1 \text{ F} = 96487 \text{ C mol}^{-1}$)
questions.solution:
The standard Gibbs free energy change is given by the relation:

$\Delta G^{\circ} = -nFE^{\circ}_{\text{cell}}$

For the given reaction, the number of electrons transferred is $n = 3$.

Substituting the given values:

$\Delta G^{\circ} = -3 \times 96487 \text{ C mol}^{-1} \times 1.54 \text{ V}$

$\Delta G^{\circ} = -445769.94 \text{ J mol}^{-1}$

$\Delta G^{\circ} \approx -445.77 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$

Answer: $-445.77 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
For the given hypothetical reaction:
$2\mathrm{P} + 5\mathrm{Q} \rightarrow 3\mathrm{R} + 4\mathrm{S}$
The rate of disappearance of $\mathrm{P}$ is $4 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{~mol} \mathrm{~L}^{-1} \mathrm{~s}^{-1}$. The overall rate of the reaction and the concentration of $\mathrm{S}$ formed in an interval of 20 seconds will be, respectively:
questions.solution:
For the given reaction $2\mathrm{P} + 5\mathrm{Q} \rightarrow 3\mathrm{R} + 4\mathrm{S}$, the overall rate of reaction is given by:

$\text{Rate} = -\dfrac{1}{2} \dfrac{d[\mathrm{P}]}{dt} = \dfrac{1}{4} \dfrac{d[\mathrm{S}]}{dt}$

Given the rate of disappearance of $\mathrm{P}$ is $-\dfrac{d[\mathrm{P}]}{dt} = 4 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{~mol} \mathrm{~L}^{-1} \mathrm{~s}^{-1}$.

The overall rate of the reaction is:

$\text{Rate} = \dfrac{1}{2} \times (4 \times 10^{-3}) = 2 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{~mol} \mathrm{~L}^{-1} \mathrm{~s}^{-1}$

The rate of formation of $\mathrm{S}$ is:

$\dfrac{d[\mathrm{S}]}{dt} = 4 \times \text{Rate} = 4 \times (2 \times 10^{-3}) = 8 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{~mol} \mathrm{~L}^{-1} \mathrm{~s}^{-1}$

The concentration of $\mathrm{S}$ formed in an interval of $20$ seconds is:

$\Delta[\mathrm{S}] = \dfrac{d[\mathrm{S}]}{dt} \times \Delta t = (8 \times 10^{-3}) \times 20 = 160 \times 10^{-3} = 16 \times 10^{-2} \mathrm{~mol} \mathrm{~L}^{-1}$

Answer: $2 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{~mol} \mathrm{~L}^{-1} \mathrm{~s}^{-1}$ and $16 \times 10^{-2} \mathrm{~mol} \mathrm{~L}^{-1}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: When 2-bromobutane is treated with aqueous $\mathrm{KOH}$, the major product formed is $P$. When the same alkyl halide is treated with alcoholic $\mathrm{KOH}$ and heated, the major product formed is $Q$. Identify $P$ and $Q$.
questions.solution:
